name: Dijim-Bwilim
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Adelberger, Jörg & Roger Blench. 2026. The peopling of the Muri Mountains, Northern Nigeria: evidence from linguistics and ethnography. Afrikanistik-Aegyptologie-Online. doi:10.18716/ojs/aaeo/2026_12031. 47 pp.
sources.note: Ethnohistory of Cham and neighbours; no Cham phonology. Bibliography confirms Ajede 2022, 2023 conference papers as the only descriptive work on Dijim.
Says only 'A tonal language, it has a whistled register'; lists 8 vowels and 17 consonants without source; nothing on stress. Tertiary.

sources.citation: Ajede, Chika Kennedy. 2023. Nominal modification in Dijim. Slides, 2nd Adamawa Conference (Paris), 23 pp. LLACAN AdaGram project.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Slide 22 'NP and tones': head nouns fall into two tonal classes in the NP (Type 1 changes to LL, Type 2 no change); data fully tone-marked with H, L, falling and downstep. Treats Dijim as a tone language.

sources.citation: Litvinova, Lora & Chika Kennedy Ajede. 2023. Quotative constructions in Kugama and Dijim. Slides, workshop 'Reported discourse within grammar' (Villejuif), 24 pp.
Ajede, Chika Kennedy. 2022. Morphological classes and genders in Dijim. Slides, 52nd Colloquium on African Languages and Linguistics (CALL), Leiden, 28 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; tone-marked data, notes ATR vowel harmony and vowel elision only. States that before 2020 'very little was known about the language' (Jungraithmayr 1968-69 a few dozen words; Kleinewillinghöfer 2014 an 18-word list).

sources.citation: Elstermann, Julius-Maximilian. 2021. Nominale Klassifikation im Tula-Waja: Erste Schritte zur Rekonstruktion des Genus-Systems im Tula. MA thesis, Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin, 185 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on Dijim prosody; cites a few Dijim forms from secondary data; remarks (p.19-20) that no tone analysis exists even for Tula.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2020. Adamawa. In R. Vossen & G. Dimmendaal (eds.), The Oxford Handbook of African Languages, 220-230. Oxford: OUP.
sources.note: Handbook chapter with a phonology paragraph for NW Adamawa/Tula-Waja languages (tone, possibly accent); second-hand at best for Dijim.

sources.citation: LLACAN AdaGram project page 'Dijim' (Chika Kennedy Ajede),https://llacan.cnrs.fr/AdaGram/dijim.html,and Ajede's LLACAN staff page (PhD project since 2020: 'Grammatical analysis and documentation of Dijim (Bwilim)').
sources.note: No prosodic statement; lists all prior work (Jungraithmayr 1968-69, Kleinewillinghöfer 2014, Elstermann 2021) and Ajede's talks.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2014 (ms.). Tula-Waja Group: 100-wordlist. Adamawa Languages Project, Mainz. 11 pp. (scan; columns CA = Dijim, CAm = Bwilim).
sources.note: Wordlist only (scanned of p.1 confirms abbreviations + references, then lexical rows); no statement on tone or stress.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2014. The languages of the Tula-Waja Group (web pages, Adamawa Languages Project, JGU Mainz), incl. 'Tula-Waja: Pronouns and Numbers' (1 p. PDF).
sources.note: Classification, dialects (Dijim of Kindiyo, Bwilim of Mɔna, Loojaa variant), noun-class notes; no discussion of tone or stress.

sources.citation: Adelberger, Jörg. n.d. The Cham: A collection of ethnographic and historical data from fieldwork 1989-1993 (Ethnographic and Historical Profiles of the Peoples of the Muri Mountains). 43 pp. LLACAN AdaGram site.
sources.note: Ethnography; language only classified (Waja group); nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 1996. Die nordwestlichen Adamawa-Sprachen - Eine Übersicht. Frankfurter Afrikanistische Blätter 8: 80-103.

sources.note: Group overview by the main fieldworker on Tula-Waja (field notes 1985-1995 include Dijim and Bwilim); may contain general prosodic remarks for the group.

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann. 1968/1969. Class Languages of Tangale-Waja District (Bauchi Province, Northern Nigeria). Afrika und Übersee 52: 161-204.

sources.note: Earliest linguistic notes on Cham (a few dozen words plus class morphology) alongside Tula, Waja, Dadiya etc; may contain a brief remark on tone/accent transcription. AuÜ vols 1-92 not digitized.

sources.citation: Ajede, Chika Kennedy. in prep. (PhD, EPHE-PSL / LLACAN, begun 2020; supervisors Van de Velde & Idiatov, AdaGram). Grammatical analysis and documentation of Dijim (Bwilim).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only full description of the language ever undertaken; its phonology chapter will contain the tone system and any statement on stress/accent (AdaGram grammars, e.g. Lesage 2020 on Kam, treat stem-initial accent explicitly). Not yet in theses.fr or HAL as of 2026-09-17; ask author (ajedechikakennedy2@gmail.com) or LLACAN for the phonology chapter.
